Learn to explain how to talk about loading data when a SwiftUI view appears and stopping it when the view goes away: Load on Appear, Automatic Cancellation & task(id:), with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
Load on Appear - Starting a view's data loading at the moment the view shows on screen.

Load on Appear - Starting a view's data loading at the moment the view shows on screen.
한국어: Load on Appear: 뷰가 화면에 나타나는 순간 데이터 로딩을 시작하는 것

task(id:) - A SwiftUI modifier that restarts its task whenever the given value changes.

landscape.hook: Can you explain Load on Appear, Automatic Cancellation and task(id:) in English?

dialogue.title: Load data when the view appears

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, I start my loading in the view's initializer, and it feels wrong.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: It is. Do the load on appear instead, with the `task` modifier.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: It starts async work when the view appears. That is load on appear in SwiftUI.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: And when the user goes back before the request ends?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: SwiftUI cancels the task by itself. That is automatic cancellation.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So I do not need to cancel by hand?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Right. But your code must still react to cancellation.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Now my screen has a filter. How do I reload when it changes?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Use task(id:) and pass the filter. The task restarts when the value changes.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: And the old task is cancelled first?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes, thanks to automatic cancellation. Then task(id:) starts the new one.
Do the load on appear, not in the initializer.
